Bochnia Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bochnia, Poland

Not demolished. NOTE: the source page's community-history narrative for this record appears to actually describe nearby Brzesko (settlement from 1605, 1921 population figures matching Brzesko records), not Bochnia - likely another instance of mismatched content between adjacent town pages in the source database. What follows uses only facts specific to this cemetery itself. The cemetery, likely established in the early 19th century (confirmed by tombstones dated 1828 and 1835), holds the graves of tzaddikim Arie Lejbusz Lipszyc (d. 1846) and Meszulam Zalman Jehonatan (d. 1855), and Rabbi Efraim Templer (d. 1935). A WWI military section (War Cemetery No. 275) holds 21 Austro-Hungarian soldiers. On June 18, 1942, Germans shot about 200 people here. The last known burial occurred in 1960 (Jadwiga Ziarnecka, born Sala Ebenholz). Postwar restoration included a 1947 Holocaust memorial, ohel reconstructions in the 1960s and 1990s, and two additional mass-grave monuments erected in 2017-2018; local volunteer Anna Brzyska has led ongoing site care.
